lines.text: Sarah wants eggs. Not Friday's eggs. Today's.
This farm sells the day's eggs until midnight. Buy them at breakfast, collect them at dinner. Claim them or lose them.
Two eggs, forty-two sats. A real Lightning invoice.
And nobody presses pay. The farm settles its own invoice. It is a demo, remember.
Paid. Two claims mint, locked to Sarah's wallet.
Two bearer claims. Whoever holds the code owns the eggs. So Sarah moves them to the portal.
Same farm, one link. Any device opens the claims portal.
The code pastes in. The claim reads: two eggs, today.
One tap. No teller code, no operator. The eggs simply arrive, on the screen.
A receipt, like any vending machine. The claims are burned, and the day's window has used them up.
The public ledger agrees. Two redeemed, capacity intact, no names anywhere.
Signet sats in, imaginary eggs out. The machine is the counter. NUT-32, live.
